title: Texas-Style Beef Ribs
subtitle: Massive bones, pepper crust, smoke
description: Massive bones, pepper crust, smoke. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Season the beef ribs
steps.instruction: Pull silver skin if present. Coat ribs with salt and pepper (heavy — Texas style). Let sit 30 minutes while smoker preheats to 275°F with oak.

steps.title: Smoke until tender
steps.instruction: Smoke bone-side down 6–8 hours until meat pulls back from bone and internal temp reads 200–205°F. Wrap in butcher paper if bark gets too dark before tenderness. Meat should jiggle when you shake the rack.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest 20 minutes tented with foil. Cut between bones. Hold on sheet trays at 180°F — beef ribs dry out fast, so keep a backup pan lightly spritzed with broth.

steps.title: Serve on the line
steps.instruction: Pile ribs on sheet trays with extra pepper on the side. Backup pan in a warm oven — do not cover tightly or bark softens.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
tonightSpread: Plate Texas-Style Beef Ribs with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Texas-Style Beef Ribs on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
Slice proteins on a cutting board at the end of the line so everyone sees the smoke ring and char.
Set sauce and pickles on the side — sauced meat holds better on the backup tray.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Massive bones, pepper crust, smoke. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
